title: NHL Logo Quiz: Hard Mode
headline: Can You Name The NHL Team From A Tiny Piece Of Its Logo?
description: A hard NHL logo quiz: eight tiny pieces of NHL team logos, about 2% of each logo. Guess the team, tap to reveal the answer, keep score and share your result.
intro: Every piece below is a small square cut from an NHL team crest, about one fiftieth of the whole mark. No team names, no giveaway animals. Each piece still holds one real detail, a color pair, a feather or an edge that only one club owns.
Make your guess, then tap Show The Answer. Be honest and mark whether you got it, and your score adds up at the bottom.

items.fact: The orca logo arrived in 1997, drawn so the whale's body curls into a C for Canucks.

items.piece: The red maple leaf behind the silver jet.
items.fact: When the NHL came back to Winnipeg in 2011, the new Jets logo borrowed the look of the Royal Canadian Air Force roundel.

items.piece: The tips of the feathers at the end of the wing.
items.fact: The winged wheel is a nod to Detroit as the Motor City. It has been the club's logo since it became the Red Wings in 1932.

items.piece: The wheat-colored river at the bottom of the forest scene.
items.fact: The Wild logo is a forest scene that doubles as the head of a wild animal: the North Star is its eye and the river is its mouth.

items.piece: The colored feathers in the headdress.
items.fact: Founder Frederic McLaughlin named the team after his World War I Army unit, the 86th Blackhawk Division.

items.piece: The top end of the S.
items.fact: Seattle's S is a nod to the Seattle Metropolitans, the first American team to win the Stanley Cup, in 1917.

items.piece: The penguin's hockey stick crossing the yellow triangle.
items.fact: The yellow triangle behind the skating penguin stands for the Golden Triangle, downtown Pittsburgh.

items.piece: The bottom of the LEAFS lettering and a vein of the leaf.
items.fact: The 2016 leaf has 31 points at the top for the 1931 opening of Maple Leaf Gardens and 17 veins for the club's 1917 founding.
